title: GridForge Spreadsheet — Harbor Task Rework QC
subtitle: Re-check of the 2026-08-25 tracker after instruction, rubric, packaging, and verifier changes.
note: Static rework QC completed 2026-08-26. The latest available oracle used an older 27-criterion rubric and scored 0.9808; the current 19-criterion task still requires a fresh oracle run.

tasks.name: GridForge
tasks.headline: 16 prior findings rechecked: 15 fixed and 1 partial; one new blocker remains until the rewritten task passes a fresh oracle run.

findings.what: Prior finding: save-to-session user binding was graded but not stated.
findings.why: The reworked brief now says every view has its own editing session tied to its selected seeded user, and server saves must match it.
findings.impact: The previously private identity invariant is now part of the task contract.

findings.what: Prior finding: the judge named the golden-only window.gridforgeSessionId global.
findings.why: The literal is gone. The prompt now requires discovery from an observed legitimate save and forbids assuming a global, cookie, header, or field name.
findings.impact: Correct alternative session implementations are no longer coupled to the oracle's JavaScript shape.

findings.what: Prior finding: overlapping identity probes received contradictory verdicts and made the score irreproducible.
findings.why: Workbook/stale probes and session/user probes now live in separate criteria with explicit per-probe evidence tables.
findings.impact: The same identity behavior is no longer independently and inconsistently scored twice.
findings.fix: No further change required; confirm with the fresh oracle run.
findings.action: Verify both rows during the next oracle run.

findings.what: Prior finding: mandatory find/replace behavior was not graded.
findings.why: A dedicated 1.0-weight criterion now checks navigation, wraparound, current replacement, Replace All, Undo, and Redo.
findings.impact: The feature now contributes to the training signal.

findings.what: Prior finding: two high-weight formula checks depended on the same B2/dropdown geometry collision.
findings.why: The reworked criteria use distinct cells and workflows: B2/C2, B3/C3, I10, H22 and F22:F24. Suggestions are graded at the cell being edited.
findings.impact: One positional collision no longer determines multiple independent formula scores.

findings.location: tests/rubric/browser/browser.toml and prompt.md — direct save probes
findings.what: Prior finding: large conjunctive criteria passed without executing every probe.
findings.why: Probe families were separated, and every remaining matrix now requires an explicit numbered status/body/equality table; prompt.md says an omitted probe fails.
findings.impact: Partial execution is visible and cannot silently become a pass under the written grading contract.
findings.fix: No static change required; inspect the next oracle reasoning table.
findings.action: Confirm complete tables in the fresh run.

findings.what: Prior finding: shipped executable modes were absent.
findings.why: solve.sh and test.sh are now tracked as 100755, but test.py remains 100644. test.py is invoked explicitly through python3, so this remaining mode is non-blocking.
findings.impact: The actual Harbor entry scripts are executable; only the directly interpreted Python helper remains non-executable.
findings.fix: Optionally mark tests/test.py executable before packaging for complete closure.

findings.what: Prior finding: node_modules, databases, sidecars, and bytecode shipped with the task.
findings.why: Those files are absent from the current solution tree, and artifact collection excludes node_modules and database files.
findings.impact: The deliverable and collected model app are reviewable and no longer dominated by generated files.

findings.what: Prior finding: a private Windows toolchain path shipped in the solution.
findings.why: run-local.cmd has been removed from the task tree.
findings.impact: The client bundle no longer exposes irrelevant local tooling layout.
findings.action: Keep the file out of the upload.

findings.what: Prior finding: /app artifact collection failed on the model submission.
findings.why: Artifact collection now excludes node_modules and database files while retaining the application source.
findings.impact: Future job bundles should retain reviewable model output without size/file-count failure.
findings.fix: Confirm status=ok in the next run manifest.

findings.what: Prior finding: the hard manifest gate used unstated filename and route-count conventions.
findings.why: The brief now requires a .db/.sqlite/.sqlite3 SQLite path and the main workbook and revision routes, matching the deterministic parser's extension and two-route expectations.
findings.impact: A zero-score manifest gate now enforces a stated contract.
findings.action: Keep manifest wording and parser aligned.

findings.what: Prior finding: mixed range-plus-cell function arguments were graded but not stated.
findings.why: The brief now says functions accept the usual combinations of values, cells, and ranges.
findings.impact: The multi-argument calculation criterion is supported without exposing its exact test formula.

findings.what: Prior finding: agent and verifier each had six-hour budgets despite much shorter observed runs.
findings.why: Budgets are now 2 hours for the agent and 4 hours for the verifier, with RewardKit capped at 3.5 hours; prior worst observed verification was about 85 minutes.
findings.impact: Hung runs no longer consume six hours per phase while retaining substantial headroom.
findings.action: Reassess only if the current 19-criterion run exceeds the new budget.

findings.location: tests/rubric/browser/browser.toml — navigation, clipboard, fill and history criteria
findings.what: Prior finding: several explicitly required spreadsheet behaviors were not asserted.
findings.why: The current rubric checks the full navigation key sequence, TSV/CSV paste plus copy/cut, both fill directions, cell-history timestamps, and arithmetic operators. The concise brief groups these as normal spreadsheet behavior.
findings.impact: The former coverage gaps now have direct scoring evidence.

findings.what: Prior finding: distant anchor scrolling was duplicated across two weighted criteria.
findings.why: The first-load criterion no longer repeats A14/A40/A80. Distant-row integrity remains only in the autosave/reload persistence journey.
findings.impact: Broken long scrolling no longer loses weight twice for the same check.
findings.action: Keep anchors in the persistence criterion only.

findings.what: Prior finding: mixed CRLF/LF islands obscured rework provenance.
findings.why: The task now includes a .gitattributes rule enforcing LF for text files.
findings.impact: Future checkouts and archives have stable line endings and cleaner diffs.
findings.fix: Normalize once during the next commit if Git reports residual working-tree churn.
findings.action: Confirm the final archive uses LF.

findings.what: The current 19-criterion reworked task has no matching clean oracle run. The latest available oracle used an older 27-criterion rubric and scored 0.9808 rather than 1.0.
findings.why: An oracle below 1.0 is a ship blocker, and an older run cannot prove a materially rewritten rubric and instruction set.
findings.impact: The task is not yet proven solvable under the exact verifier that would ship.
findings.fix: Run the oracle on the current folder, investigate any failed row, and require 1.0 before running the model or shipping.
findings.action: Provide an OpenRouter key to run the current oracle.

blocks.title: Ship blocker
items: GF-17: obtain a 1.0 oracle result against the current 19-criterion task before treating this rework as complete.

blocks.title: What is strong
items: Session discovery is implementation-agnostic and no longer names a golden-only JavaScript global.
SQLite startup/restart idempotence and reward-on-crash safeguards remain deterministic.
Server rejection criteria use observed same-origin request replay and verify non-mutation.
The instruction set is now split by topic and reads like a product brief without dropping the graded feature families.
